summary.headline: Max Estates Q1 FY27 pre-sales of about Rs 1,100 crore (5x YoY), with consol PAT of Rs 8 crore on Rs 52 crore revenue.
summary.overview: Pre-sales rose 5x YoY to about Rs 1,100 crore, anchored by the full sellout of Phase-1 of the Terraces at Estate 361 (about Rs 500 crore) plus Rs 600 crore of sustenance sales. Collections were about Rs 575 crore, and management said these fund construction without incremental debt on residential projects. Consolidated revenue was Rs 52 crore, EBITDA Rs 8 crore, PBT Rs 11 crore and PAT Rs 8 crore, with the P&L reflecting only a fraction of the contracted portfolio. ICRA assigned a first-time A+ (stable) issuer rating on a consolidated basis. Management declined to give FY27 sales guidance, though it did guide collections and deployment figures.

financial_highlights.metric: Lease rental income (Max Towers, Max House, Max Square)
Gross debt (incl. LRD borrowings of Rs 934 crore)

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Pre-sales about Rs 1,100 crore, with Estate 361 Terraces Phase-1 (GDV Rs 500 crore) fully sold out and sustenance sales of Rs 600 crore. Management said about 50% of sales came from new launches and 50% from sustenance.

segments.name: Commercial annuity (Max Towers, Max House, Max Square)
segments.commentary: 100% occupancy across three operating assets; lease rental income Rs 40 crore, up 5% YoY. Latest Max Towers lease at Rs 156/sq ft/month vs weighted average Rs 132, a mark-to-market upside of over 50%.

segments.name: Max Asset Services
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 15 crore in Q1, up 16% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 collections guided to Rs 2,500-2,700 crore (earlier call: Rs 2,500-3,000 crore), with about half from already-sold projects reaching construction milestones and half from fresh sales.
FY27 project deployment of about Rs 1,500-1,800 crore, leaving OCF of about Rs 750-1,000 crore for business development.
H2 FY27 new launches of about Rs 5,000-5,500 crore, plus Rs 3,000-4,000 crore of already-launched unsold inventory for sustenance sales.
Sector 59 (Golf Course Extension Road, GDV above Rs 3,500 crore) expected to launch in Q3 FY27; management has not decided whether to launch it in phases.

Max Square 2 (1 mn sq ft) OC expected by Q2 FY28, adding about Rs 125 crore to annuity; Max District (1.6 mn sq ft) OC in Q3 FY28 and Q3 FY29, adding about Rs 200 crore; combined annual rental of about Rs 700 crore at peak occupancy.
Management is not giving pre-sales guidance for FY27, citing volatile micro-economic conditions.
capex_capacity: Remaining equity and debt capex on commercial assets is Rs 1,500-1,800 crore, described as fully tied up; financial closure achieved on all commercial assets with SBI and ICICI debt sanctioned.
Long-term strategy is about 40% equity and the rest debt on commercial projects; construction finance converts to lease rental discounting on commissioning.
Under-construction commercial assets: Max Square 2, Max District and Max One.
Annual target of 2 mn sq ft of residential development additions.
Estate 105 (Noida) GDV revised up to Rs 6,000 crore on a residential mix; Phase-2 to launch in FY27.
Max One (Delhi One redevelopment): 2.5 mn sq ft, GDV about Rs 3,200 crore, annuity Rs 145 crore; sold at Rs 37,000/sq ft ex-GST, described as the highest in Noida.
demand_pricing: Delhi NCR recorded about 8,800 residential launches in Q2 CY26 (Gurgaon about 70%); about 18,500 units in H1 CY26.
Residential weighted average prices broadly stable QoQ; sales volumes across the sector moderated through the quarter.
Delhi NCR office leasing of 4.1 mn sq ft in Q2 CY26.

Pre-leasing at Max District (about 200,000 sq ft) and Max One (about 100,000 sq ft) at 25-30% premium; pipeline above 3 mn sq ft under discussion. Max Square 2 LOI for about 90,000 sq ft at 25% premium; Max District LOI for 200,000 sq ft at 35% premium.

Antara-branded senior living units sell at about a 7-10% (management also cited ~10%) premium to Max Estates units; development management fee to Antara is about 9.5% of topline on the Antara portion.
Embedded value: Rs 17,500 crore total revenue potential on launched portfolio, of which Rs 13,500 crore sold and contracted (Rs 3,500 crore collected); embedded PBT Rs 4,500-5,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and marketing expense rise sharply YoY in Q1, and how should quarterly cost run-rate and EBITDA margins be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Nitin Kansal said Ind AS 115 recognises residential sales at possession while all advertising and marketing cost is expensed as incurred. Q1 had launches and ongoing sales effort versus no launches in the year-ago quarter, so costs look elevated. Future spend will track the launch schedule for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Which of Estate 361 Phase-2, Estate 105 Phase-2 and Sector 59 will be the biggest FY27 pre-sales contributor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to single out one project, saying the three are expected to contribute roughly equally, as they sit in different micro-markets (Dwarka Expressway, Golf Course Extension Road, Noida).

qa_highlights.question: How does the Antara arrangement work commercially, and what is the revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Sahil Vachani said Max India and Max Estates are separate listed companies. Estate 360 and 361 sit on Max Estates' balance sheet, with Antara as development manager at about 9.5% of topline on the Antara-branded portion. Nitin Kansal said senior living units sell at a 7-10% premium, and an Rs 5 crore senior living apartment would pay Rs 45-48 lakh as fee, collected over the project life.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY27 collections guidance of Rs 2,500-3,000 crore still valid given Q1 collections, and will OCF stay positive as construction ramps?
qa_highlights.answer: Sahil Vachani narrowed collections guidance to Rs 2,500-2,700 crore, split equally between already-sold projects reaching construction milestones and fresh sales. Deployment on projects is Rs 1,500-1,800 crore, leaving OCF of Rs 750-1,000 crore for business development.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the company stopped giving pre-sales guidance, and is the Sector 59 launch to be phased?
qa_highlights.answer: Sahil Vachani said guidance in the current volatile micro-economic environment is not good for long-term health, so the company will not give sales guidance. On Sector 59, the phasing decision will be taken closer to launch, though the entire project has approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the remaining commercial capex and how will it affect the balance sheet and cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Kansal said financial closure is done on all commercial assets, with SBI and ICICI debt sanctioned. Remaining capital is Rs 1,500-1,800 crore, fully tied up. Sahil Vachani said the equity portion has been provided for, the long-term split is about 40% equity and the rest debt, and construction finance converts to lease rental discounting on commissioning.

risks_watch: Net debt rose in Q1 as construction finance drawn on commercial assets (Max Square 2, Max District, Max One) increased gross debt; management said the Rs 1,500 crore incremental debt is not yet on the balance sheet, so track gross debt and LRD conversion on commissioning.
Collections guidance was trimmed to Rs 2,500-2,700 crore from Rs 2,500-3,000 crore, and no pre-sales guidance is being given for FY27, so visibility on sales velocity is limited.
Sector 59 (GDV above Rs 3,500 crore) launch in Q3 FY27 and undecided phasing; about Rs 12,000 crore of new launches planned in FY27 depend on market conditions.
Antara fee (about 9.5% of topline on the Antara portion) is commercially negotiated and not fixed; the fee could change, and Antara-linked projects are decided case by case.
Management said sector sales volumes moderated through the quarter, and peers report leasing deferrals; watch pre-leasing premiums (25-35%) and whether the Rs 3,000 mn sq ft pipeline converts.
Delhi Master Plan 2047 land pooling and BD opportunities in Ghaziabad are still early; no timelines or deal parameters were given.
key_quotes: We do believe that we firmly operate in that category where from a product differentiation perspective, from a brand recognition perspective, we do believe that we will be able to command very strong sales
We feel that giving guidance in the current microeconomic environment is not the best thing for the long-term health of the company and we are very focused on the quality of sales that we do
It is a dynamic thing. It is a commercial transaction between two commercial entities.

So we remain very confident on the strength of the product, on the strength of the brand, on the pull that we have on our geographical diversification and on our product diversification to continue the growth trajectory for Max Estates at large.
summary.management_tone: Confident on brand, pipeline and collections, with a strong tone on the Q1 pre-sales and ICRA rating. Cautious and evasive on forward sales: management declined to guide pre-sales for FY27 and gave no detail on Ghaziabad deal terms or Delhi land pooling timelines, citing volatile micro-economics and competitive sensitivity.
